testing-object-state.label: Testing Object State
testing-object-state.summary: Write executable `assert` tests that prove starting state, rejected state changes, and repeated transitions on real objects.

sketch0.title: Assert state before and after a method call

try_testing_object_state_sketch0.title: Write a before-and-after Book state test
try_testing_object_state_sketch0.prompt: `models/book.py` is already complete. In `tests/check_book.py`, use the existing `book` object to write an assertion that it starts available, call `book.checkout()`, then write an assertion that the same object's `available` state is false. Leave the model file unchanged. The test script must still finish by printing `book state tests passed`.
try_testing_object_state_sketch0.hint: Use `assert` for both observable states; the method call belongs between those two claims.

help.concept: A state-change test proves the object's state before and after the mutating method.

help.concept: Testing both branches distinguishes the validation rule from a constructor that simply stores every input unchanged.

help.hint_2: The invalid task should expose priority 0.

try_testing_object_state_sketch2.title: Write a repeated state-transition test
try_testing_object_state_sketch2.prompt: `models/counter.py` is already complete. In `tests/check_counter.py`, use the existing `counter` object to assert its count is `0`, call `increment()` and assert `1`, then call `increment()` again and assert `2`. Use the same object for the whole sequence. Leave the model unchanged and keep the final `counter sequence tests passed` print.
try_testing_object_state_sketch2.hint: The important part is the sequence: 0 → increment → 1 → increment → 2 on one instance.

help.concept: A repeated-transition test catches bugs that only appear after the same object changes state more than once.
help.hint_1: Start with an assertion before any method call.
help.hint_2: Assert again after each increment on the same counter.

q-testing-object-state-single-1.title: What should an object-state test check after a mutating method runs?
q-testing-object-state-single-1.prompt: A `checkout()` method is supposed to change a book from available to unavailable. Which test idea best proves that state change happened?
q-testing-object-state-single-1.hint: Look for the choice that checks the attribute after the method call, not just that the method exists.

help.concept: A state-change test should verify the actual attribute value after a mutating method runs, because the goal is to prove behavior, not just structure.
help.hint_1: A method can exist and still fail to update the object's data correctly.
help.hint_2: Choose the option that inspects the `available` attribute after calling `checkout()`.

options.a: Create a Book object and check that `available` becomes `False` after calling `checkout()`
options.b: Only check that the `Book` class has a `checkout` method name
options.c: Print the object once and assume the method worked
options.d: Check only the book title because constructors are more important than methods

q-testing-object-state-multi-1.title: Choose the strongest constructor validation checks
q-testing-object-state-multi-1.prompt: A `Task` constructor should keep positive priorities unchanged and replace negative priorities with `0`. Which assertions belong in a good test set? Choose all that apply.
q-testing-object-state-multi-1.hint: Include one check for valid input and one for invalid input.

help.concept: Good validation coverage includes both the normal path and the edge-case path so the constructor rule is tested from more than one angle.
help.hint_1: One correct option should confirm that a positive priority stays the same.
help.hint_2: Another correct option should confirm that a negative priority does not remain negative after construction.

q-testing-object-state-multi-2.title: Spot useful object-state edge cases
q-testing-object-state-multi-2.prompt: You are testing a `Counter` object with an `increment()` method. Which checks help prove repeated state changes work correctly? Choose all that apply.
q-testing-object-state-multi-2.hint: Think about what happens before any increments and after more than one increment.

help.concept: Repeated state-change tests are stronger when they verify the initial state and multiple successive updates on the same object.
help.hint_1: One correct option should check the starting count before any method calls.
help.hint_2: Another correct option should check the count after the method has been called more than once on the same instance.

options.a: Assert that a new counter starts at `0`
options.b: Assert that the same counter reaches `2` after two `increment()` calls
options.c: Only check that `increment` is spelled correctly
options.d: Create two separate counters and ignore their `count` values

testing-object-state-sketch-0.title: A state test should make an executable claim
testing-object-state-sketch-0.bodyMarkdown:
A state test should make an executable claim before and after a method call.

```python
lamp = Lamp()

assert lamp.on is False

lamp.turn_on()

assert lamp.on is True
```

The first assertion proves the starting state. The second proves the observable state transition.

A print statement can show a value, but an assertion automatically fails when the behavior is wrong.

testing-object-state-sketch-1.title: Validation tests need a normal case and a rejected case
testing-object-state-sketch-1.bodyMarkdown:
A validation rule needs tests for both the accepted and corrected or rejected path.

```python
normal = Score(8)
invalid = Score(-3)

assert normal.points == 8
assert invalid.points == 0
```

Testing only a normal value would not prove that negative input is handled correctly.

Choose cases that distinguish the intended validation rule from a broken implementation.

testing-object-state-sketch-2.title: Sequence tests keep checking the same object's state
testing-object-state-sketch-2.bodyMarkdown:
Some state bugs appear only after the same object changes more than once.

```python
meter = Meter()

assert meter.value == 0

meter.advance()
assert meter.value == 1

meter.advance()
assert meter.value == 2
```

This sequence proves that state accumulates correctly on one instance.

Creating a fresh object for every assertion would miss bugs that appear only after repeated calls.
